cells.tense: The strength you carry is holding your line today, in the open.
cells.act: carry on with the version you chose through another week of doubt
cells.ask: Take the version you already settled on and continue it one more week, doubt and all. Don't reopen the choice. Let Friday look like Monday.
cells.core:
You can keep a thing going when it gets heavy, and you can do it without an audience. The strength here is yours — not borrowed, not borrowed back — and it stays with you through pressure that would loosen most grips. Where it shows is plain: you go where you said you'd go, and the week doesn't get to talk you out of it.

Doubt keeps tugging at what you picked. Not the whole plan, just the next stretch. So take the one you already chose and run it another week, no re-deciding. The doubt stays. It just doesn't get to move the line this time. You'll learn whether the thing you picked holds steady, or whether it only looked right on the day you chose it.
cells.sheetLine: You hold your line when the weight pushes. It stays yours.
cells.verb: hold a chosen course through material pressure
cells.place: in the direction you are choosing

cells.tense: You will be bracing for a test that has not arrived yet.
cells.act: let the exchange with someone run both ways
cells.ask: When you pass something to someone, accept what comes back — the offered help, the answer, the rest. Let that exchange run both directions, once.
cells.core:
You hold on hard, and that hardness is real strength. But some of it runs past the thing. You're already bearing next month's weight today, and the end of it doesn't get to land — the hard part gets lived before it has any right to be here. Aimed at a future that hasn't happened, gripping turns into squeezing. Gripping harder won't fix that.

Try the other direction on something small. When you pass something to someone, accept what comes back — the favour, the help, the rest. One exchange, both sides. You'll notice how much heavier a load is when you insist on being the only one who carries it. And that you didn't have to be.

cells.tense: You have been at a door that is already behind you.
cells.act: do the giving in the open this time, where it was always done unseen
cells.ask: Do something you usually do quietly for someone where they can see you do it. No speech, no explanation. Let them watch once, and nothing more.
cells.core:
Your hand on a course isn't gone. It's folded away. You keep the staying, the tending, the giving — and nobody sees a hand in it, including you. The strength is still there, but it isn't holding anything up. What got hard was being seen doing it, not the doing.

So put some of it where eyes can reach. Choose something you usually do unseen and do it where the person it's for can watch. No speech, no explaining, no ceremony. Let one pair of eyes land on you doing it. That's the size of the act. You don't have to know yet whether it counts. Let someone else count it first.
cells.sheetLine: You gave from behind a door that's already closed.

cells.tense: You are still following something you have not told yourself about.
cells.act: go on toward it without needing a sign
cells.ask: Take the step you already decided on and do it without checking for a sign first. No permission, no confirmation. One move, then notice you didn't need it.
cells.core:
You're still going. Quietly, no announcement, the direction you set a while back — and if anyone asked, you'd say you're just doing the next thing. That's the misattribution: your hand is on the rudder and you're calling it circumstance.

The credit comes back a step at a time, not by deciding to be a certain kind of person. Take the move you'd already chosen and go — no checking for a sign, no confirmation. You'll see afterward that the sign you kept waiting for was going to be you. The radiance at the end belongs to what you kept building, and the one standing there is the one who kept going.
cells.sheetLine: You keep the course and call it circumstance.
